attribution.note: Marcus's own words on his own Substack, stating his own position.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'if my 2020 article is correct' antecedent, the full list of knowledge types and the necessity claim for formal reasoning. It is a conditional, theoretical claim about what is necessary.

contract.note: The contract correctly keeps the antecedent and refuses to score the consequent on its own. Marcus does not say which parts of the 2020 article must hold, so the result depends on an interpretation he did not supply.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional claim about necessity, and its antecedent (that his 2020 article is correct) is unspecified and unestablished. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored. The packet has no evidence items, and the necessity claim has no defined test for scope or formal reasoning.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats the significance and staffing judgments as hedged and subjective, so no plain-reading score applies. The start of the period (2022) is the evaluator's convention, not Marcus's.

evidence.note: Dated 2023 I-JEPA preprint with LeCun as an author. It confirms background JEPA work but says nothing on staffing or significance.

V-JEPA 2 preprint from June 2025, before the post, reporting benchmark results and a robot-planning demo. It shows outputs existed but cannot objectively refute a hedged 'don't seem earth-shaking' judgment.
Meta's own blog post (a company disclosure) acknowledging a single-time-scale limitation. Background balance only, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: The background fact that LeCun worked on JEPA at Meta is documented (e1, e2). But the substance of the claim, 'not a whole lot to show' and papers that 'don't seem earth-shaking', is a hedged, subjective judgment with no objective standard. Team size is also hedged with 'appears'. The V-JEPA 2 outputs do not settle a judgment about how significant they seem, so the claim is not scored.
